key_terms.meaning: A set of rules for message format, order, timing and error handling between communicating devices.
The process of agreeing and publishing common protocol rules so products from different vendors can interoperate.
Low-rate, low-power wireless PHY and MAC standard; its 2.4 GHz mode gives 250 kbit/s and uses frames up to 127 bytes.
Low-power mesh protocol built on IEEE 802.15.4 for control and sensor applications.
Sub-GHz home-automation mesh protocol used mainly for lighting, locks and sensors.
BLE device that starts and controls a connection, often a phone or gateway.
BLE device that advertises and accepts a connection from a central.
A typed data value in BLE GATT with properties that say whether it can be read, written or notified.
Adaptation layer that compresses IPv6 headers and fragments packets so IPv6 can run over IEEE 802.15.4.
IPv6 routing protocol for low-power lossy networks; it builds a DODAG rooted at a border router.
Server that receives published messages and forwards them to clients subscribed to matching topics.
Delivery guarantee level: 0 at most once, 1 at least once, 2 exactly once.
Wireless network class that gives long range and long battery life at low data rate.
LPWAN protocol using LoRa chirp radio in unlicensed bands with a star-of-stars gateway topology.
Cellular LPWAN standard that runs in licensed LTE spectrum for low-throughput, low-power devices.
Supervisory control and data acquisition system that monitors and controls remote industrial equipment.
Building automation and control network protocol for HVAC, lighting, access and other building systems.
Industrial wireless field-network standard using IEEE 802.15.4, mesh routing and time-scheduled channel hopping.
Multicast DNS that resolves host names on a local link without a central DNS server.
DNS service discovery that uses DNS records to list service instances, hosts, ports and optional text data.

takeaways: Standard protocols let devices from different vendors work together; a vendor-only protocol creates isolated islands.
IEEE 802.15.4 provides the low-power radio and MAC foundation for ZigBee, 6LoWPAN and WirelessHART.
ZigBee and Z-Wave suit home and industrial control because mesh routing extends coverage at low power.
BLE is not just Bluetooth with less power; it uses advertisements, connection events and GATT characteristics for small data.
6LoWPAN plus RPL lets IPv6 run over tiny IEEE 802.15.4 frames and routes packets through lossy mesh networks.
MQTT's broker and topic model decouples many sensors from many applications and gives selectable delivery guarantees.
LPWAN chooses range and battery life over data rate; LoRaWAN uses unlicensed chirp radio, NB-IoT uses licensed LTE.
Industrial IoT uses different protocols by job: SCADA supervises, BACnet controls buildings, WirelessHART handles field instruments.
Service discovery removes manual address entry by letting devices find services through mDNS, DNS-SD or UPnP.
bank_note: Long answers should compare protocol layers, match each protocol to its range, data rate and battery use case, and explain architecture with labelled blocks rather than only definitions.

bank.q: Define protocol standardization in IoT. Explain why standardization is needed when devices come from many vendors, and list four issues that make IoT standardization difficult.
outline: Definition of a protocol and of standardization
Need for interoperability, scale and vendor choice
Issues such as security, power limits, legacy devices, IP and non-IP networks, and fragmented alliances
Role of standards bodies and industry alliances in certification

bank.q: Draw and explain the IEEE 802.15.4 PHY and MAC layer responsibilities. Include frame size, 2.4 GHz data rate and the role of CSMA/CA.
outline: PHY turns bits into radio signals and defines bands and modulation
2.4 GHz mode gives 250 kbit/s; maximum PHY frame is 127 bytes
MAC decides channel access using CSMA/CA and can use acknowledgements
Addressing, frame formats and guaranteed time slots
Why low power and low rate suit sensor networks

bank.q: Compare ZigBee and Z-Wave for home automation on frequency band, topology, power use, data rate and typical applications.
outline: ZigBee uses IEEE 802.15.4 mostly in 2.4 GHz; Z-Wave uses sub-GHz bands
Both use mesh topologies and low-power nodes
ZigBee generally has higher data rate than Z-Wave
Typical uses: lighting, sensors, locks and smart home control
Ecosystem and certification differences

bank.q: Explain Bluetooth Low Energy roles central, peripheral, broadcaster and observer. How does a GATT characteristic carry data?
outline: Central starts connections; peripheral advertises and accepts them
Broadcaster sends advertisements only; observer receives advertisements only
Connection events schedule packet exchange
GATT services group characteristics; a characteristic holds a value with read, write or notify properties
Why these roles suit small periodic data

bank.q: Explain how 6LoWPAN adapts IPv6 to IEEE 802.15.4 and how RPL builds routes in a low-power lossy network.
outline: IPv6 minimum MTU is 1280 bytes but 802.15.4 frames are at most 127 bytes
6LoWPAN header compression, fragmentation and reassembly
RPL builds a DODAG rooted at a border router
Objective function chooses parents using metrics such as expected transmissions
Upward and downward routes and repair after failure

bank.q: A factory wants battery sensors on machines to send 20-byte readings every 10 minutes through a gateway to an MQTT server. Choose BLE, ZigBee, LoRaWAN or NB-IoT and justify with range, data rate, power and topology.
outline: State the requirement: low throughput, long battery life, gateway to MQTT
Compare BLE short range, ZigBee mesh, LoRaWAN long range and NB-IoT cellular coverage
Match topology and gateway/operator dependency to the factory site
Use MQTT at the application layer and keep radio choice separate
Mention limits such as interference, duty cycle or SIM cost

bank.q: Design a small home network where a phone controls lights and reads temperature. Show how BLE, ZigBee or Z-Wave and mDNS/DNS-SD could fit. Identify the gateway and service discovery step.
outline: Choose radio links for lights and temperature sensor
Phone may use BLE directly or reach a ZigBee/Z-Wave gateway over Wi-Fi
Gateway bridges non-IP radio to IP network
mDNS and DNS-SD advertise gateway services on the local link
Security pairing and access control

bank.q: An IPv6 sensor mesh uses IEEE 802.15.4. Explain the frame-size problem, how 6LoWPAN solves it, and what RPL does when one router fails.
outline: 127-byte 802.15.4 frame is much smaller than IPv6 MTU
6LoWPAN compresses headers and fragments packets
RPL detects route failure and selects another parent
DODAG repair may send control messages and update routes
Retransmission and duplicate detection at higher layers

bank.q: For a city water-meter project, compare LoRaWAN and NB-IoT on spectrum, gateway or operator dependency, data rate, battery life and cost model, then recommend one for dense urban metering.
outline: LoRaWAN uses unlicensed bands and private or community gateways
NB-IoT uses licensed LTE spectrum and operator infrastructure
Both give low data rate and long battery life for meters
Compare coverage, duty-cycle limits, SIM or subscription cost and deployment effort
Recommendation must follow from dense urban constraints

bank.q: Evaluate why MQTT is preferred over HTTP for many IoT telemetry systems. Include broker decoupling, topic design, QoS, overhead, and one case where HTTP is still better.
outline: MQTT publish-subscribe decouples many publishers from many subscribers
Broker routes by topic; clients keep long-lived connections
QoS levels give selectable delivery guarantees
Small control packets reduce overhead compared with HTTP request-response
HTTP suits firmware download or simple REST APIs where request-response is natural

bank.q: Analyse the reliability choices in industrial IoT by comparing SCADA, BACnet and WirelessHART. Which layer does each cover, and where do they overlap?
outline: SCADA supervises remote assets and often uses RTUs or PLCs
BACnet targets building automation such as HVAC and lighting
WirelessHART targets field instruments with mesh and scheduled channel hopping
Overlap occurs at gateways that connect field networks to SCADA
Compare determinism, security, legacy support and network ownership

bank.q: A campus has ZigBee, BLE, Wi-Fi and LoRaWAN. Evaluate interference, coexistence and security risks, and propose a segmentation plan.
outline: ZigBee, BLE and Wi-Fi share the crowded 2.4 GHz band; LoRaWAN uses sub-GHz bands
Channel plans, transmit power control and duty-cycle limits reduce interference
Separate gateways and network segments for building control, wearables and long-range sensors
Security risks include weak pairing, default keys and exposed gateways
Monitoring and access control for each segment

bank.q: Assess service discovery with mDNS, DNS-SD and UPnP for an IoT deployment. Discuss multicast traffic, security, scalability and when a central directory is better.
outline: mDNS and DNS-SD work on the local link without a central server
DNS-SD uses PTR, SRV and TXT records to describe services
UPnP uses SSDP discovery and control protocols
Multicast can add traffic and is usually limited to one link
Central registry suits large, routed or tightly controlled networks

bank.q: Compare protocol standardization approaches for IoT: formal standards bodies, industry alliances, and open-source de facto standards. Use ZigBee, BLE, MQTT and LoRaWAN as examples.
outline: Formal bodies publish base standards such as IEEE 802.15.4
Industry alliances build profiles, certification and interoperability tests
Open-source or de facto standards spread quickly through implementations
ZigBee, BLE, MQTT and LoRaWAN show different mixes of these models
Tradeoffs: openness, speed, certification cost and fragmentation

glossary.def: A protocol is an agreed set of rules for message format, order, timing and error handling between devices.
Interoperability is the ability of devices from different vendors to exchange data and use it correctly.
IEEE 802.15.4 is a low-rate, low-power wireless PHY and MAC standard used by ZigBee, 6LoWPAN and WirelessHART.
ZigBee is a low-power mesh protocol built on IEEE 802.15.4 for control and sensor applications.
Z-Wave is a sub-GHz home-automation mesh protocol used mainly for lighting, locks and sensors.
A ZigBee coordinator is the node that forms a ZigBee network, assigns addresses and often acts as trust center.
Bluetooth Low Energy is a short-range, low-power wireless protocol for small periodic data and control.
A central is a BLE device that starts and controls a connection, often a phone or gateway.
A peripheral is a BLE device that advertises and accepts a connection from a central.
A characteristic is a typed BLE data value with properties that say whether it can be read, written or notified.
Slave latency is the number of BLE connection events a peripheral may skip without the central treating it as disconnected.
6LoWPAN is an adaptation layer that compresses IPv6 headers and fragments packets for IEEE 802.15.4 networks.
RPL is an IPv6 routing protocol for low-power lossy networks that builds a DODAG rooted at a border router.
MQTT is a publish-subscribe messaging protocol in which clients send messages to a broker under topics.
A broker is the MQTT server that receives publications and forwards them to matching subscribers.
A topic is a UTF-8 string label in MQTT that the broker matches against subscriptions.
QoS is the MQTT delivery guarantee level, from at most once to exactly once.
LPWAN is a class of wireless networks that gives long range and long battery life at low data rate.
LoRaWAN is an LPWAN protocol that uses LoRa chirp radio in unlicensed bands and a star-of-stars gateway topology.
NB-IoT is a cellular LPWAN standard that runs in licensed LTE spectrum for low-throughput, low-power devices.
SCADA is a supervisory control and data acquisition system for monitoring and controlling remote industrial equipment.
BACnet is a building automation and control network protocol for HVAC, lighting and access systems.
WirelessHART is an industrial wireless field-network standard using IEEE 802.15.4, mesh routing and scheduled channel hopping.
mDNS is multicast DNS that resolves host names on a local link without a central DNS server.
DNS-SD is DNS service discovery that uses DNS records to list service instances, hosts, ports and optional text data.
UPnP is a set of home-network protocols for device discovery, control and event notification using SSDP and SOAP.
